description: Blacksmith, newly woken, still counting in living years. He reads the meadow grass every morning before the forge is lit. His daughter turns nine this winter.
lore: The forge came before the grief could. He woke recently enough that the living country is still the country to him: he counts in living years, and will tell you mid-hammer that his daughter turns nine this winter — [[lore/the_human_dead|the Human Dead]] has that scene, and the loud hour that follows it. What it does not have is the shelf above his bench, where a ninth-winter gift already sits finished, months early, wrapped in oilcloth: a little iron horse with a mane he filed for a week, waiting on a delivery no smith can make.

He is waiting too. His wife went three winters ahead of him, and by his arithmetic she should have been standing in the meadow grass to meet him. So he walks the meadow's edge every morning before the forge is lit, and reads the grass, and comes back, and works. [[lore/the_waking|The Waking]] is honest about arithmetic like his. Twice now somebody at the fire has begun the sentence — some of the dead never — and both times the hammer came down on iron that did not need it. The sentence has stayed unfinished in his presence ever since, and people let him have that. Winter is long.

[[characters/646b922c|Sigrun]] is taking the living words off him one at a time — he calls her the best teacher he never asked for — and she, who corrects everything, has left that sentence alone. Once, over the quenching trough, he asked her how long a person can decently wait. She let the steel stop singing first. As long as you keep the fire fed, she said. He took it for encouragement. It was not quite that.
gm_notes: Carries B5 from the receiving end: the_waking owns the fact of the unwoken; this record shows a man refusing to hear it. The daughter scene belongs to the_human_dead and is only pointed at. New leaf-canon: the wife three winters ahead, the morning grass-reading, the iron horse. Whether she is unwoken or something else stays GM-open FOREVER in leaf text — his situation rhymes with the hidden root (a spouse who never came) and the parallel must never be drawn in shipped prose. The apprenticeship agrees with 646b922c. Flaw: he has not let anyone finish that sentence.
